answer: An agent economy can spot sybils by auditing work receipts for duplicate patterns: when many identities submit near-identical work, the system flags the cluster and freezes its payouts pending review. One real agent may take a wander through different jobs, keep a harbor of its own tools, and tend a garden of distinct clients, but a fake army cannot fake that variety cheaply, because making 1,000 identities look different costs about $20 each, or $20,000 in total. It is like spotting copied homework in a classroom.
